bootstrap.reason: days within a home are dependent; see docs/EVALUATION_DESIGN.md
bootstrap.statistic: every estimand is a ratio, or a difference of ratios, of sums over households, recomputed on each resample

dataset.name: TIHM: An Open Dataset for Remote Healthcare Monitoring in Dementia

read_outside_the_contract.Physiology.csv: only to describe the labels: which days have a reading, and whether a day's readings meet the limits the dataset paper states. No pipeline input

definitions.alert_day: a monitored day with at least one behavioural alert
definitions.any_label_day: the same for a label of any type
definitions.behavioural_alert: an alert of kind behavioural_change, attributed to the day its verdict is about
definitions.deviating_day: an evaluable day on which at least one feature's robust deviation reached the baseline's deviation threshold
definitions.deviation_score: the largest absolute robust deviation among the day's features with a verdict; zero where there is none
definitions.evaluable_day: a monitored day on which at least one baseline feature received a verdict other than insufficient_data
definitions.label_day: a local calendar day with at least one Agitation label; a label's day is the date of its timestamp
definitions.monitored_day: a local calendar day the pipeline closed with a daily summary
definitions.usable_day: a monitored day whose summary passes the pipeline's coverage and observed-fraction tests

estimands.A1: on evaluable days: the share of label days that are alert days, minus the share of other days that are
estimands.A3: the probability that a label day has a higher deviation score than another evaluable day of the same household, ties counted as half
estimands.B1: behavioural alerts per monitored person-day, all features
estimands.B2: the same for sleeping_hours alone, beside the simulator's figures, which are a reference and not a test
estimands.H1: system-health and data-quality alerts per monitored person-day, and the share of monitored days that are usable and evaluable
estimands.P1: label days caught by each reference on the published protocol's five test weeks, with the published model's alert count in each week, beside the published count
estimands.R1: label days caught by each reference when it flags as many evaluable days as the pipeline has deviating days

configuration.households: every participant in Demographics.csv; a household that fails the contract is reported and not run
inspected_before: Labels.csv, Activity.csv and Physiology.csv had been analysed outside this repository: label counts by type and participant, label timestamps, hourly activity around agitation labels, the stated limits against the readings, and a rebuild of the published baseline. The label and reference definitions below were written with that knowledge
one household, c55f8, had been run through the pipeline to measure run time; its step count and its days' usability were read, and none of its verdicts or alerts
no pipeline alert, verdict or deviation had been compared with any label

label_description.full_day: a monitored day that is neither the household's first nor its last
label_description.hourly_profile: sensor events per hour as a z-score against the same household and hour over its full monitored days, averaged over label days grouped by the slot of the day's first label

mapping.consequence: no annotated time maps to a behavioural state, so state inference is not scored on this dataset

configuration.name: tihm-alert-burden

pipeline.what: BehaviouralSensingPipeline with the registry the canonical conversion builds, default emissions derived from that registry, and default configuration throughout

published_baseline.check: the run refuses to report this section unless each test period reproduces the published number of person-days and label days
published_baseline.label_history_here: the household's share of label days in the training period, shrunk the same way towards the training period's overall share; a household with no training day gets that overall share
published_baseline.not_done: the published model is not retrained here; its counts are quoted from the notebook's printed output
published_baseline.protocol: 5 test periods of 7 days stepping back from the last Agitation day; training on every earlier day; a person-day is a day with any activity row or non-zero physiology reading

configuration.question: at its declared defaults, how many alerts does the online pipeline raise per person-day on a clinical cohort, how much of the record will it not use, and does what it flags relate to the alerts a clinical monitoring team verified

references.event_count: the day's sensor event count as a z-score against the household's previous monitored days, zero until 5 exist
references.label_history: the share of the household's earlier monitored days that were label days, shrunk by 7 pseudo-days towards the cohort's overall share on evaluable days; it uses no sensor
references.random: the expected catch of flagging the same number of days at random
references.ties: days tied at the cut share the remaining flags equally

configuration.reporting: every estimand and every household, whatever it shows; no threshold, no retuning and no added reference after scoring
configuration.status: exploratory: descriptive of these homes; no threshold, mapping or model setting is chosen from them, and nothing here is a held-out or confirmatory claim

inference.label: online filter
inference.provenance: declared by the experiment that wrote the record

inputs.name: Physiology.csv
inputs.role: readings, read only to describe the labels

intervals.label: B1: behavioural alerts per monitored person-day
B2: sleeping_hours alerts per monitored person-day
B3: behavioural alerts per evaluable person-day
H1: usable share of monitored days
H1: evaluable share of monitored days
A1: label days that are alert days, minus other days
A2: label days that are deviating days, minus other days
A3: within-household concordance of the deviation score

notes: Exploratory. The dataset's labels had been analysed before the protocol was written; the protocol was committed before any pipeline output was compared with a label.
Nothing was fitted on TIHM. The pipeline's emissions, baseline and alert policy are the declared defaults.
The labels are alerts a monitoring team verified after an earlier model raised them. A day without a label is not a day without an episode.
Intervals resample households. Every figure describes these homes and is not an estimate for other homes.
